comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: The control plane is connection-per-request: herdr answers a request and closes the socket, so every intent Muster dispatches pays a connect() (docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 6). That belongs in the input-to-glyph budget, and it is a per-intent cost rather than a per-byte one, so it scales with interaction rate rather than output volume.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Half landed. ./dev --perf measures and gates the per-byte and per-key budgets in release, against a checked-in baseline, with a 2x tolerance and a loud failure when a benchmark stops running. Verified it fails by doctoring the baseline: regression, vanished benchmark and new benchmark all reported correctly.

Still open, and now printed by the harness itself rather than left implicit:
- mirror.apply (ns/event), the control plane's per-event cost - needs the mirror (a_26DAm1Zt0).
- render at 15 panes - per-byte cost is linear and covered; what 15 panes actually tests is aggregate scheduling across surfaces, which needs splits (a_26BJGL7VZ).

The input-to-glyph half is answered separately by ./dev --latency and a_26BIX28HG.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
mirror.apply is measured and in the baseline at 231 ns/event. Remaining debt is render at 15 panes, which needs splits (a_26BJGL7VZ) and is printed as not-measured rather than dropped.

New cost worth budgeting when splits land: agent state costs one held-open connection per pane, so 15 panes is 16 connections and 16 threads. Nothing measures that yet.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: The 'fast is a feature' desideratum needs a standing measurement, not a one-off. Measure at the same injected edges the test harness uses (architecture.md, seams and test hooks): input-to-glyph latency, per-event core work, per-frame render cost - at 1 and 15 panes, local and over SSH. Fails the build on regression once a baseline exists. Distinct from the stage-1 double-emulation spike, which answers 'is this viable at all'; this answers 'did we just make it worse'.
title: Perf harness: budget input-to-glyph at 1 and 15 panes
